newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-DISCARDED BLACK ATTACKS BRITISH SELECTORS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-DISCARDED BLACK ATTACKS BRITISH SELECTORS.

text.p: Olympic silver medallist Roger Black launched a fierce attack on British athletics chiefs on Tuesday after they left him out of the individual 400 metres for next month's world championships.
Black, who missed last weekend's national trials in Birmingham because he of a virus, has only been selected for the 4x400 relay squad for the Athens event.

Black, one of Britain's most prominent athletes who last month took over from former Olympic sprint champion Linford Christie as captain of the national team, was livid that he had learned of decision first in the British media.
"I heard it through the media. I don't deserve that sort of treatment," he said. "It is bad man management. It doesn't take a lot. It is just good communications. That is important in life."
"It is if they are saying we don't respect the illness."

Jamie Baulch, who took a 4x400 relay silver medal in Atlanta with Black, was selected ahead of the former world silver medallist and European champion who had wanted to prove his fitness at a race in Belgium this weekend.
Baulch, who finished third in the trials and won a silver medal at the world indoor championships in Paris in March, was selected with automatic choices Iwan Thomas and Mark Richardson.
Britain does not have such a strict selection procedure as the United States where only athletes who compete in the nationals trials are picked for the team. There is more flexibility.
But the decision to leave out Black was one of the most controversial since 800 metres joint world record holder Sebastian Coe was not included in the team for the 1988 Seoul Olympics.

The issue was big news in the British media. Both Black and national coach Malcolm Arnold spoke on one prestigious BBC radio programme which normally deals with major politicians rather than sportsmen.
Arnold said the British team manager had tried to speak to Black through his coach.
"We had to make a decision. Unfortunately Roger is not there because of his physical state," Arnold said.
"Selection has to be according to current form. Baulch has the better current form. What sort of message would we have sent to Jamie Baulch if we had left him out? We have to live with that."

British athletics is struggling to find new names at the moment with Christie in the twilight of his career and no sign of major prospects coming through in the middle-distance events to replace the likes of Coe and his 1980s rival Steve Ovett.
Black is one of the few figures in the team who is known to British sports fans who do not follow athletics closely.
